verses.1: LORD, why do you stand at a distance? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?
verses.2: In the arrogance of the wicked, the poor are driven to despair; they are snared by the schemes they have devised.
verses.3: For the wicked boasts of their desires, and the greedy curse the LORD.
verses.4: The wicked, in their pride, say, “God will not seek it out; there is no God in all their thoughts.”
verses.5: Their ways are always secure; your judgments are far from them. They scoff at their foes and think they are safe.
verses.6: They say in their hearts, “We will not be shaken. We will not know trouble, for we will never lack.”
verses.7: Their mouths are full of lies; their tongues speak only deceit. Their words are smooth, but inside they are full of violence.
verses.8: They lie in wait in the open square; in secret they murder the innocent. Their eyes are watchful, ever on the lookout for the helpless.
verses.9: They lurk in the shadows like a lion in its den, lying in wait to seize the poor. They seize the poor and drag them into their net.
verses.10: They fall into their own traps, and their feet are caught in their snares.
verses.11: They say to themselves, “God has forgotten; he has hidden his face; he will never see.”
verses.12: Arise, LORD! Lift up your hand, O God. Do not forget the afflicted.
verses.13: Why does the wicked despise God? He says in his heart, “You will not call him to account.”
verses.14: You have seen the suffering of the helpless, O LORD; you have taken notice of their distress. You have placed the helpless in your hand; you are the helper of the orphan.
verses.15: Break the arm of the wicked and the evildoer; call their iniquity to account until you find none.
verses.16: The LORD reigns forever and ever. The nations will perish from his land.
verses.17: You, O LORD, have heard the longing of the poor; you will prepare their hearts. You will incline your ear to them.
verses.18: To judge the orphan and the oppressed, so that human beings no longer may threaten them on earth.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The question “why do you stand at a distance?” reflects the psalmist’s sense of divine absence.
- v. 4: “There is no God in all their thoughts” translates the idea that the wicked do not acknowledge or consider the divine.
- v. 11: “They say to themselves” is used to clarify that the denial of God’s presence is internal to the wicked.
- v. 15: “Call their iniquity to account until you find none” reflects the Hebrew for a complete eradication of wrongdoing.
